before: Project boundaries could preserve sprint state, audit facts, and reviewed knowledge, but there was no canonical close-time record of the capability delta itself or of who had authority to ratify that claim.
after: A validated governed prototype now lets an intentional close distinguish a proposed capability boundary from routine activity, write an unpublished delta bound to exact evidence and file bytes, and stop at an operator-directed procedural ratification boundary.

evidence.observation: The v1 contract separates draft, procedurally attested ratification, supersession, and publication states; it rejects mutable revision aliases, scoring fields, and draft publication without claiming to authenticate a person.

The shared skill requires a sprint-close receipt to bind to an existing database-local close event, then governs evidence collection, unpublished storage, validation, digest-only event linkage, and the operator ratification boundary.
Sprintctl selects the shared capability-receipt skill, declares the close-boundary lifecycle as a verification risk surface, and leaves the value judgment outside its database and CLI contracts.
The consumer contract records only a pointer and digest in sprint history and explicitly excludes maintenance auto-close from eligible receipt boundaries.

counterfactual: Without this operating change, future capability claims would continue to be reconstructed from repositories, sprint records, and prose after the fact rather than compared with a preserved boundary record.
transfer: Sprintctl now selects the shared close-time receipt workflow and documents its authority and storage boundaries.
dependency: Repositories must continue to invoke the shared sprint-close path instead of bypassing it.
The workspace _artifacts tree must be backed up and remain available across environment changes.
A human operator must review proposed deltas and create append-only ratified successors rather than treating drafts as settled claims.
The schema, validator, and source-reference conventions must be maintained as tools and providers change.
belief_changed: The existing sprint-close workflow and shared artifact tree were sufficient for the first longitudinal layer; a new database, service, score, or Cockpit write path was not required.
displaced_alternative: Unknown: no contemporaneous record identified which specific alternative work this operating change displaced.
would_disconfirm: This governed-prototype claim would weaken if intentional closes routinely bypass the receipt decision, if a provider change or six-month pause makes drafts impossible to locate and validate, or if operators accept drafts without inspecting their evidence and unknowns.

unknowns.reason: No immutable ex-ante expectation record was created before this implementation began.
This is the first pilot receipt, so repeated use across projects and seasons has not yet been observed.
The receipt inherits the workspace artifact backup posture, which was not independently exercised by this implementation task.
No Capability Lab Assessment or public thesis update has yet been derived from ratified receipts.
